text:
erin: quick heads-up from staging load test: when a tenant's reserved pool was being drained, our immediate fallback to CPU burst caused sustained p99 regression.
mika: is this because we route all at once to whatever fallback variant is compatible?
erin: yes. operator marks reservation as gone -> controller flips routes -> boom. No intermediate check.
ravi: we should be deliberate: progressive evaluation + circuit breaker. sample a small percentage through the candidate fallback before switching everyone.
mika: agree. propose 3 mechanisms: sampling evaluation, progressive ramp with health checks, and a hard circuit that refuses fallback if p99 exceeds threshold.
erin: sketch policy (YAML) for operator and tenant config: 
```yaml
fallback_evaluation:
  sampling_rate: 0.07 # start with 7%
  sample_duration_s: 20
  success_criteria:
    p99_ratio: 1.8 # fallback p99 must be < 1.8x primary p99
    p50_ratio: 1.4
    error_rate_delta: 0.004
  ramp_steps_percent: [20, 50, 100]
  ramp_delay_s: 8
  fallback_order: [gpu-small, cpu]
  oscillation_protection:
    window_s: 60
    max_toggle: 3
```
mika: fallback_order means operator will try smaller GPU slices first, then CPU-only. important for QoE when small-GPU packing is available.
ravi: operationally, who decides to promote from sampling -> ramp? operator should emit a short-lived evaluation metric and controller or control-plane can call promote. But automatic mode is handy.
lee: suggest operator run automatic promote when evaluation passes, but emit evaluation_{id} and an event. console can abort/promote manually.
ops-bot: created incident INC-4527 and task TASK-331.
erin: API proposal: POST /v1/reservations/{id}/fallbacks start|abort|promote body {policy} -> returns eval_id. GET /v1/evals/{eval_id} status.
ravi: RBAC: only platform-admin or tenant-admin can trigger abort/promote. read should be wide.
mika: telemetry: operator must push metrics: fallback.eval.start, fallback.eval.success_rate, fallback.eval.p99_ratio, fallback.ramp.step, fallback.oscillation_count with tenant tag.
lee: alerting: add prom rule when fallback.oscillation_count > 3 in 5m or fallback.eval.p99_ratio > 2.5.
erin: testing: unit tests for sampler, integration test with fake small-gpu availability and CPU fallback, and a staged chaos run where we kill nodes to trigger drain.
ravi: also add a safety NACK: if evaluation fails catastrophically, operator should return standardized HTTP 503 with x-redwood-fallback-reason so clients can degrade gracefully.
mika: UX: console should show active evals with p50/p95/p99 graphs and a single-click abort/promote. Add tooltip explaining risk.
lee: edge case: what if fallback_order contains gpu-small but cluster fragmentation prevents placement mid-ramp? operator should check packability per step and skip to next item if insufficient capacity.
erin: add policy flag allow_partial_packing: false by default; if true, operator will accept degraded slice packing and continue.
ravi: action items: TASK-401 (operator: eval engine + metrics), TASK-402 (controller: progressive ramp wiring), TASK-403 (console: eval UX + RBAC), TASK-404 (tests + chaos scenarios).
erin: volunteers? ravi takes TASK-401, lee takes TASK-402, mika takes TASK-403, i'll own TASK-404.
ops-bot: tasks created: TASK-401,TASK-402,TASK-403,TASK-404.
erin: I'll add a short note to the autoscale RFC follow-up doc with the policy snippet and link to INC-4527.
lee: once ravi posts proto/payload for eval endpoints i'll review and we can iterate on telemetry labels.
ravi: will draft proto + CR by tomorrow.
mika: thanks all — this should stop surprise p99 spikes during maintenance. :thumbsup:
